The '''2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 127th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland championship]] since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The draw for the 2014 fixtures took place on 3 October 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/fixtures-for-2014-allireland-hurling-and-football-championships-revealed-29632518.html|title= Fixtures for 2014 All-Ireland hurling and football Championships revealed|date=4 October 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=4 October 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url =https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/winners-of-cork-and-waterford-clash-to-face-clare-in-2014-munster-senior-hurling-championship-609001.html|title=Winners of Cork and Waterford to face Clare in 2014|date=4 October 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 October 2013}}</ref> The championship began on 27 April 2014 and ended on 7 September 2014.

On 7 June 2014 [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] versus [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] was broadcast on [[Sky Sports]], the first time a Championship fixture was broadcast live to a UK-wide audience.<ref>{{cite news|first=Seán|last=Moran|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-aiming-to-put-on-a-show-for-new-sky-audience-1.1823632|title=Kilkenny aiming to put on a show for new Sky audience: Daunting task facing Brian Whelahan's Offaly at Nowlan Park|newspaper=The Irish Times|date=7 June 2014|access-date=7 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://gaabanter.ie/5-ways-uk-will-react-hurling-sky-sports/ |title=5 Ways the UK will React to Hurling on Sky Sports |work=Hon the Banter |date=2 June 2014 |access-date=2 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140625143851/http://gaabanter.ie/5-ways-uk-will-react-hurling-sky-sports/ |archive-date=25 June 2014 }}</ref> British viewers were reported to have been "amazed and confused", "bemused but impressed" and "amused and confounded" after seeing [[hurling]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite news|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien|url=http://www.livegaelic.com/features/definative-guide-british-reaction-hurling/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713160506/http://livegaelic.com/features/definative-guide-british-reaction-hurling/|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 July 2014|title=The Definitive Guide to the British Reaction to Hurling|work=Live Gaelic|date=8 June 2014|access-date=8 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/captivated-but-confused-british-twitter-users-react-to-hurling-on-sky-sports-30337841.html|title=Captivated but confused... British twitter users react to hurling on Sky Sports|work=Sunday Independent|publisher=Independent News & Media|date=8 June 2014|access-date=8 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thescore.ie/11-british-based-tweeters-hurling-sky-sports-1505468-Jun2014/ |title=11 British-based tweeters who can't believe that hurling is a thing |work=The Score |date=8 June 2014 |access-date=8 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610133549/http://www.thescore.ie/11-british-based-tweeters-hurling-sky-sports-1505468-Jun2014/ |archive-date=10 June 2014 }}</ref>

[[Clare GAA|Clare]] entered the championship as [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|defending champions]], however, they were defeated by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20244741.html|title=A day borrowed from the hurling gods|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=30 September 2013|access-date=1 October 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the All-Ireland title following a 2–17 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] after a replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/power-and-the-glory-go-to-kilkenny-1.1944305|title=Power and the glory go to Kilkenny |publisher=Irish Times|date=27 September 2014|access-date=28 September 2014|first=Malachy|last=Clerkin}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2014/1024/654593-column-the-hurling-year-2014/|title= Column: The Hurling Year 2014|date= 24 October 2014 |work=	RTÉ Sport|access-date=28 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/mullane-the-moments-that-made-this-years-championship-special-30640412.html|title=  Mullane: The moments that made this year's Championship special|date= 6 October 2014 |work=	Irish Independent|access-date=28 October 2014}}</ref>

==Overview==

All teams from the [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013 championship]] continued to line out in hurling's top tier in 2014.

On 23 March 2013, the GAA's annual Congress adopted a proposal from the Central Competition Controls Committee (CCCC) which sought to introduce a round-robin qualifying group in Leinster for five designated counties.

Ten counties competed in the 2013 Leinster championship; however, the CCCC proposal decreased the Leinster competition to a field of five regulars, namely [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]], [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]], [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Galway GAA|Galway]], alongside two more from a round-robin qualifying group featuring [[Laois GAA|Laois]], [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]], [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]], [[London GAA|London]] and [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]]. These five teams each played four games, with the top two qualifying for the Leinster Championship quarter-finals. The fourth-placed team met the winner of the [[Christy Ring Cup]] in a promotion/relegation play-off. The bottom county faced automatic relegation to the Christy Ring Cup.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/gaa-play-it-safe-with-provincial-hurling-format-reform-29023155.html|title=GAA play it safe with provincial hurling format reform|work=Irish Independent|access-date=1 April 2013|date=27 January 2013|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/new-hurling-championship-structure-accepted-at-congress-1.1336873|title=New hurling championship structure accepted at congress|work=Irish Times|access-date=1 April 2013|date=23 March 2013|first=Seán|last=Moran}}</ref>

==Broadcasting==
In the first year of a deal running from 2014 until 2016, a total of 45 provincial and All-Ireland championship matches in hurling and football were broadcast live on television in Ireland.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/off-the-ball/gaa-must-be-cautious-after-reaching-for-sky-30146908.html|title= GAA must be cautious after reaching for Sky|date=1 April 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0104141419-media-rights-press-release/ |title=Media Rights Press Release |date=2 April 2014 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=2 April 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140403204043/http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0104141419-media-rights-press-release |archive-date=3 April 2014 }}</ref>
A total of 31 games will be shown by [[RTÉ]] and 14 by [[Sky Sports]] for the first time. [[TV3 (Ireland)|TV3]]'s six year-involvement with broadcasting games came to an end in 2013. Sky Sports will also broadcast live the All-Ireland Hurling and Football semi-finals and finals along with RTÉ.
<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/sky-sports-in-tv3-out-as-gaa-announces-new-broadcasting-package-30145793.html|title= Sky Sports in, TV3 out as GAA announces new broadcasting package|date=1 April 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/this-is-not-the-thin-end-of-the-wedge-its-the-whole-wedge-30146924.html|title= This is not the thin end of the wedge, it's the whole wedge|date=2 April 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/oneill-nervous-over-deal-with-sky-264008.html|title= O'Neill 'nervous' over deal with Sky|date=2 April 2014|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/masters-of-hype-must-convince-masses-264014.html|title= Masters of hype must convince masses|date=2 April 2014|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2014/0401/606028-gaa-rights-deal/|title= RTÉ & Sky secure GAA rights, RTÉ in worldwide deal|date=2 April 2014|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=2 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/rte-and-sky-reveal-gaa-schedules-ahead-of-opening-weekend-of-live-coverage-30273866.html|title=RTE and Sky reveal GAA schedules ahead of opening weekend of live coverage|date=14 May 2014|work=Irish Independent |access-date=14 May 2014}}</ref>

The first game to be broadcast by Sky Sports was the Leinster quarter-final between Kilkenny and Offaly in Nowlan Park on Saturday 7 June.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/sky-sports-gaa-debut-to-feature-kilkennys-roofless-stand-264945.html|title=Sky Sports' GAA debut to feature Kilkenny's roofless stand|date=10 April 2014|work=Irish Examiner |access-date=10 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-offaly-sky-sports-live-1504844-Jun2014/ |title=As It Happened: Sky Sports makes GAA debut – Leinster SHC, Kilkenny v Offaly |date=7 June 2014 |work=The Score |access-date=10 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610024610/http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-offaly-sky-sports-live-1504844-Jun2014/ |archive-date=10 June 2014 }}</ref>
[[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]] were announced as presenters of Sky's coverage, with Dave McIntyre and Mike Finnerty as commentators.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/sky-play-it-safe-with-bigname-analysts-30287224.html|title=Sky play it safe with big-name analysts|date=19 May 2014|work=Irish Independent |access-date=20 May 2014}}</ref> Analysts for the hurling championship were [[Jamesie O'Connor]] and [[Nicky English]].<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/sky-sports-announces-gaa-coverage-team-630961.html|title=Sky Sports announces GAA coverage team|date=19 May 2014|work=Irish Examiner |access-date=20 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/carney-we-will-bring-gizmos-and-gadgets-to-our-gaa-coverage-30285676.html|title=Carney: We will bring gizmos and gadgets to our GAA coverage|date=19 May 2014|work=Irish Independent |access-date=20 May 2014}}</ref>

In May, the GAA and RTÉ launched a new streaming service called ''[[GAAGO]]'' intended to stream championship games worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaago-launched-to-stream-live-and-ondemand-games-worldwide-30274506.html|title= GAAGO launched to stream live and on-demand games worldwide|date=14 May 2014|work=Irish Independent |access-date=16 May 2014}}</ref>
The subscription-based service will be available to fans everywhere in the world outside of the island of Ireland, including all the games broadcast in Ireland exclusively by Sky Sports.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/1405140906-gaa-go-launch/ |title=GAA and RTE Digital launch GAAGO |date=14 May 2014 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=16 May 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517114629/http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/1405140906-gaa-go-launch/ |archive-date=17 May 2014 }}</ref>
All 45 televised games from the football and hurling championships, as broadcast by both RTÉ and Sky will be available to watch on GAAGO.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2014/0514/617212-gaago-launched-by-gaa-and-rte/|title= GAAGO to stream up to 45 games per year worldwide|date=15 May 2014|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=16 May 2014}}</ref>
For Great Britain, the games broadcast by Sky will only be available through Sky.
The price for a worldwide GAAGO 'Season Pass' is €110 while in Britain, the GB Pass will be €60. A pay-per-game option is available for €10, and this will rise to €14 for the quarter-final, semi-final and final stages of the championship.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/entertainment/tv-radio/gaa-and-rte-team-up-as-gaelic-games-go-around-the-world-30276189.html|title= GAA and RTE team up as Gaelic games go around the world|date=15 May 2014|work=Irish Independent |access-date=16 May 2014}}</ref>

The throw in time is fixed for 7.00pm and Sky Sports are already covering the Ulster football semi-final between Monaghan and Armagh with the GAA's television contracts preventing live television coverage of two championship games at the same time.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/throwin-clash-with-sky-game-scuppers-live-coverage-of-replay-30378173.html|title=Throw-in clash with Sky game scuppers live coverage of replay|date=24 June 2014|work=Irish Independent|access-date=24 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2014/0624/626272-gaa-defends-galway-v-kilkenny-scheduling/|title= GAA defends Galway v Kilkenny scheduling|date=24 June 2014|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=25 June 2014}}</ref>

== Miscellaneous ==
* Limerick's 2–18 to 2–16 Munster semi-final defeat of Tipperary was their first victory over their near neighbours at [[Semple Stadium]] since [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1973]].
* Kilkenny's tally of 5–32, or 47 points, was the biggest score the Cats have posted in a championship match during [[Brian Cody]]'s tenure as manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=217877|title=Free-scoring Cats rewrite the history books|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=8 June 2014|access-date=8 June 2014}}</ref>
*For the fourth time in five years the Munster champions were defeated in their All-Ireland semi-final.
*The aggregate score of 4–50 (62) in the drawn All-Ireland final is the largest combined tally in a championship decider since [[1970 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1970]].
*For the third year in-a-row the All-Ireland final ends in a draw.
*[[Henry Shefflin]] of Kilkenny becomes the first player to win ten All-Ireland medals on the field of play.

==Controversies==

===Involvement of the British Sky Broadcasting Group===
The decision by the GAA to grant access to satellite broadcasting company [[BSkyB]] of Championship hurling was criticised in some quarters.<ref>{{cite news|first=Mark|last=Duncan|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/social-price-paid-for-new-sky-deal-may-prove-costly-to-the-gaa-1.1749265|title=Social price paid for new Sky deal may prove costly to the GAA|newspaper=The Irish Times|date=4 April 2014|access-date=4 April 2014}}</ref> The first attempt by [[Sky Sports]] to cover live televised hurling – a Leinster Championship encounter between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] – drew an audience share of less than 10 per cent of that which tuned into the free-to-air [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]/[[Laois GAA|Laois]] encounter at Croke Park the following day.<ref>{{cite news|first=Jason|last=O'Brien|url=https://www.independent.ie/entertainment/television/tv-news/exclusive-32000-viewers-in-ireland-tune-into-skys-gaa-debut-30339999.html|title=Exclusive: 32,000 viewers in Ireland tune into Sky's GAA debut|work=Irish Independent|date=9 June 2014|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref> In addition, the match was erroneously billed in advance by Sky as a "Connacht GAA football" game.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-offaly-connacht-1499692-Jun2014/ |title=Sky Sports promo says Kilkenny v Offaly is a Connacht football game |work=The Score |date=4 June 2014 |access-date=4 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140616045915/http://www.thescore.ie/kilkenny-offaly-connacht-1499692-Jun2014/ |archive-date=16 June 2014 }}</ref>
